#9790. Building Smaller, Safer Symfony Messenger Queues With Compression and Encryption

Hi, friends, being AI enthusiast, I'm an MBA, CEO and CPO who loves building products. I share my insights here.)

Hi, friends, being AI enthusiast, I'm an MBA, CEO and CPO who loves building products. I share my insights here.)

Hi, friends, being AI enthusiast, I'm an MBA, CEO and CPO who loves building products. I share my insights here.)

Symfony Messenger serializes a message, hands the bytes to a transport and forgets about them. Two things routinely go wrong with those bytes:

mattleads/messenger-compress-bundle fixes both at the transport-serializer layer. You opt in per message with a stamp or enforce a policy per transport, and your handlers receive the same plain PHP objects they always did. We'll walk through the whole thing on a small Doctrine (SQLite) transport, because then the queue is a table you can SELECT from and see what changed.

Symfony Flex registers the bundle. Without Flex, add it yourself:

Nothing happens yet. The bundle registers a serializer service, mattleads_messenger_compress.serializer, that wraps Messenger's default serializer. Until a transport uses it, your messages are untouched.

You have two options. Start with one transport:

Or wrap the default serializer so every transport gets it:

One tip for the walkthrough only: Messenger's default serializer is PHP serialize(). If you switch the default to the JSON one, plain bodies become human-readable in the database, which makes the "before" picture much clearer:

The bundle doesn't care which one you wrap. It compresses and encrypts bytes.

Here is a message you would not want sitting in a queue table:

Dispatch it as usual and look at the row. In the demo, app:queue:inspect --grep does this. By hand it's just SQL:

The IBAN is right there. Every backup of that database has it too.

That's 32 random bytes, base64-encoded. Put it in .env.local for development and in your secrets store for production. Symfony's own vault works fine:

The body is XChaCha20-Poly1305 ciphertext (libsodium, fresh 192-bit nonce per message, authenticated). The headers are still readable: the message type, the scheme, the key id. That's deliberate: the consumer needs them to know what to do and Messenger needs the type to route the message. Which brings up the one rule worth memorizing, call it the header rule: stamps travel as headers and are not encrypted. Put secrets in the message body, never in a stamp.

Notice the size went up: 119 bytes became 212. A 24-byte nonce, a 16-byte tag and base64's 33 % overhead cost more than a tiny body saves. That's fine. Encryption is a decision about sensitivity, not about size.

If a transport only ever carries sensitive work, stop thinking about stamps:

A single message can opt out with PlainStamp. An explicit EncryptStamp always wins over policy.

Now the other problem. GenerateInvoiceBatch with 5,000 order lines serializes to 759 KB of JSON. Three ways to shrink it:

Automatically above a size. This is the default to pick, because nobody remembers to add a stamp to the one message that grows:

Two details of the automatic policies: they only keep the compressed body when it is actually smaller than the original (random blobs and already-compressed data pass through untouched) and PlainStamp opts a message out. An explicit CompressStamp is always honored even if the result is larger.

What it looks like with auto_threshold: 4096:

CompressStamp('gzip'), EncryptStamp('v2')

The third row is the common production combination: compress and encrypt. The bundle always compresses first and encrypts second regardless of the order of your stamps, because ciphertext does not compress. The 76 bytes between rows two and three are the gzip header plus the nonce and tag.

One caveat from the CRIME/BREACH family: compressed-then-encrypted length can leak information about the plaintext. If a single message mixes attacker-controlled input with a secret and the length is observable to that attacker, do not compress it. For almost every queue job this isn't a concern, but it's worth knowing.

The bundle adds up to four headers to the encoded envelope. Everything else (the type header, the stamp headers) is whatever the inner serializer produced.

Base64 is the default because the Doctrine, Redis and SQS transports all want text bodies. On AMQP you can drop it and save the 33 %:

Because everything is in headers and the body is self-describing, a consumer with the bundle installed decodes any mix of plain, compressed, encrypted and compressed-and-encrypted messages from the same queue. You can roll the bundle out to consumers first and start stamping messages later.

But the envelope your handler is wrapped in now carries a TransformedStamp describing what the serializer undid: compression, encryption, keyId, wireSize, rawSize and a ratio() helper. It implements NonSendableStampInterface, so it is never sent back out if the message is re-dispatched. A tiny listener turns it into logs or metrics:

Push ratio() and wireSize into your metrics backend tagged by message class and you've got a dashboard of what each job actually costs your broker.

Keys leak, people leave, policies say "every 90 days". Rotation is the part most home-grown encryption layers get wrong, because there's always a message in flight encrypted with the old key.

The bundle's answer is a key ring. Every encrypted message carries its key id in X-Encryption-Key-Id; consumers decode with whichever key the message names and active_key says which key new messages use.

You can watch it happen in the demo by running the producer with one key and the consumer with the other:

If active_key is omitted, the last key in the map is used.

This is the part to understand before production. Decryption is authenticated, so a message encrypted with a key the consumer doesn't have, or modified in the broker, is refused rather than handed to your handler as garbage. Let's corrupt a stored body by hand:

So: the worker doesn't crash, the handler never runs, the retry strategy you configured applies and the message is parked on the failure transport with the original bytes intact. That last point matters for the "wrong key" case. Suppose a consumer was deployed without v2 and some v2 messages failed. Add the key and replay:

The failed message is re-sent through the serializer untouched (it isn't compressed or encrypted a second time), decoded with the now-present key and handled normally.

A note on Symfony 8.1. Messenger 8.1 changed how a transport serializer must report a message it cannot decode: it has to return an envelope wrapping MessageDecodingFailedException instead of throwing, so the stamps that count retries survive. Bundle v0.1.0 threw and on 8.1 that meant "retry #1" forever with an empty failure transport. The scenario above is how I found it; v0.1.1 returns the wrapped failure. The official custom-serializer example in the Symfony docs now shows the same pattern (symfony-docs#23459) and the throwing path itself is tracked in symfony/symfony#67791, with a one-file reproducer.

The errors you can see and what they mean:

Decryption failed: authentication tag mismatch (wrong key or tampered payload).

The key with that id exists on the consumer but is different from the producer's or the body was modified.

No encryption key with id "v2" is configured. Known ids: v1.

The consumer has not received the new key yet. Rotation step 1 was skipped.

Received an encrypted message but encryption is not configured on this consumer.

encryption.enabled is false on the consumer or it has no keys.

Message requested encryption but mattleads_messenger_compress.encryption is not enabled / has no keys.

Producer side: you dispatched with EncryptStamp before configuring a key.

Unknown compression algorithm "zstd". Available: deflate, gzip.

Your handler tests do not change; they never saw the serializer. For an integration test that exercises the real round trip, the in-memory transport can run the serializer like a broker would:

Dispatch with stamps, consume, assert on the TransformedStamp of the received envelope. This is how the bundle's own functional tests work.

The bundle is on Packagist and GitHub (MIT, Symfony 6.4–8.x, PHP 8.2+). The runnable walkthrough with the inspect command, the listener and the tamper scenario is at github.com/mattleads/messenger-compress-demo.

Custom compressors (Brotli, LZ4) plug in by implementing CompressorInterface and are picked up by the mattleads_messenger_compress.compressor tag. Custom encryptors implement EncryptorInterface. If you run this against SQS, Redis or AMQP at volume, open an issue with the ratios you see and anything that surprised you. That's what the issue tracker is for.

Source Code: You can find the full implementation and follow the project's progress on GitHub: https://github.com/mattleads/messenger-compress-bundle

Holiday app marketing is mostly a deadline problem: the App Store and Google Play each have lead times, and by the time Christmas Day installs arrive, almost everything that needs a review has to be approved already. This post lays out those deadlines in order, the promotion rules on each store, and what to fix in your app before the rush of new-device owners.

The spike is driven by new hardware. People unwrap a phone or tablet, face an empty home screen and start searching the stores, browsing the Today and Apps tabs and asking friends what to get. Sensor Tower estimated roughly $277 million in consumer spending across both stores on Christmas Day 2019 alone.

That demand comes with more competition for every slot, paid ones included. The apps that do well usually finished their prep in October and November: approved product pages, scheduled events and working offer codes.

Work backwards from these dates. If you are reading this in early November, the first row is already behind you, but most of the rest is still open.

On that last row: Apple warned in December 2024 that reviews could take longer between December 20 and 26. Watch for a similar 2026 notice in late November.

Several product page changes don't need a binary update, which makes them ideal for late December:

A useful pattern is two events: one for the run-up to the holidays and one for the week after Christmas, when new owners are still exploring.

Two details worth knowing: iOS custom offer codes can act as a single shareable holiday code, and in several European countries and the UK, Play buyers see only the sale price, with no strikethrough. On iOS, mention the sale in your promotional text so people know it ends.

Someone who installs on December 25 decides during that first session whether your app stays. Before the holiday build ships:

Store featuring is crowded in December, so don't rely on it alone. Pitch gift guides, newsletters and communities that publish holiday lists, and submit to app directories and launch sites.

The cost of a will varies dramatically based on how you create it and how complex your estate is. Here is a comprehensive comparison of every method, from free options to premium attorney packages.

Several factors push will costs toward the higher end of each range:

The will vs trust decision is primarily a financial calculation: does the upfront cost of a trust save more than it costs by avoiding probate?

When you die with only a will (no trust), your estate must go through probate — a court-supervised process where a judge validates your will, your executor inventories assets, debts are paid, and remaining assets are distributed. Probate costs include:

Probate also takes 6-18 months on average and is a public proceeding — anyone can look up your will, your assets, and who inherited what.

A revocable living trust costs $1,500-$5,000 upfront but avoids probate entirely. The math is straightforward:

For most FI-focused households who are building wealth toward financial independence, the trust pays for itself many times over. If your net worth exceeds $100,000-$200,000 and you own real estate, a trust is almost certainly the better financial decision.

Even with a trust, you still need a pour-over will — a short document that catches any assets not transferred into the trust during your lifetime and directs them into the trust at death. You also still need a healthcare directive and durable power of attorney. Most estate plan packages include all four documents together.

The sticker price of a will is only part of the total cost of estate planning. Several hidden costs catch people off guard:

The FI-optimized approach to estate planning minimizes cost without sacrificing protection:

Start with an online will now. A $159 Trust & Will plan gives you a will, healthcare directive, and power of attorney today. Do not let perfect be the enemy of done — having a basic will is infinitely better than having no will while you save up for an attorney.

Upgrade to a trust when your net worth exceeds $200,000. At this point, the probate avoidance savings justify the $1,500-$3,500 cost of adding a trust.

Shop attorney fees aggressively. Estate planning is a competitive market. Get quotes from at least three attorneys. Many offer flat-fee packages, and prices can vary by 50-100% for the same work in the same city. Ask specifically whether the quote includes trust funding assistance and deed transfers.

Use online services for updates. Rather than paying an attorney $200-$500 for a codicil, many online platforms let you update your will for free or for a small annual subscription ($19-$39/year). Trust & Will, for example, includes one year of free updates.

Bundle documents. An estate plan package (will + trust + POA + healthcare directive) typically costs 20-40% less than purchasing each document separately. If you are going to see an attorney, get everything done in one engagement.

Here is the counterintuitive truth: the most expensive estate plan is the one you never create. Dying without a will (intestate) triggers state default rules that may not match your wishes, longer and more expensive probate proceedings, and potential family conflict. For parents of minor children, it means a judge — not you — decides who raises your kids. The $0-$259 cost of an online will is trivially small compared to these consequences.

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

Yes. FreeWill (freewill.com) offers a free basic will funded by nonprofit partners. Some states also accept handwritten (holographic) wills that cost nothing. Military personnel can get free wills through the JAG office on any military installation. Many bar associations and legal aid societies offer free will clinics several times per year. While these free options work for simple estates, you may want to pay $99-$259 for a more comprehensive online service that includes healthcare directives and power of attorney.

Attorneys charge $300-$750 for a simple will and $750-$1,500 for a complex will with special provisions. A complete estate plan package (will, trust, power of attorney, healthcare directive) runs $1,500-$5,000. Fees vary significantly by location — attorneys in major metros charge 2-3 times more than attorneys in smaller cities for the same work. Always ask for a flat fee rather than hourly billing for estate planning.

For straightforward estates, yes. Major online will makers like Trust & Will, Nolo WillMaker, and LegalZoom produce documents that are legally valid in all 50 states and cover the same core elements an attorney would include. The difference is that an attorney can provide customized advice, handle complex situations, and anticipate issues specific to your state law. If your estate is simple, an online will is functionally equivalent. If your situation has any complexity, the attorney consultation is worth the additional cost.

Online services typically include free updates for one year and then charge $19-$39 per year for ongoing access. An attorney charges $100-$500 for a codicil (formal amendment) or $300-$1,000 to draft a new will. For minor changes, a codicil is sufficient. For major changes (new spouse, additional children, significant asset changes), creating an entirely new will is cleaner and reduces the risk of conflicting instructions.

The most expensive part of estate planning is NOT the documents — it is probate. Probate costs 3-7% of your estate value ($15,000-$72,000 on a $500,000-$1,000,000 estate) and takes 6-18 months. By comparison, even the most expensive estate plan package ($5,000-$10,000) is a fraction of what your family would spend navigating probate without a trust. The second most expensive mistake is outdated beneficiary designations on retirement accounts, which can send six or seven figures to the wrong person with no legal recourse.

The cost of a will ranges from $0 to $10,000+ depending on your method and complexity, but the most expensive option is always having no will at all. For most FI-focused households, start with an online will for $0-$259 to get basic protection in place immediately. As your net worth grows beyond $200,000, invest $1,500-$5,000 in a comprehensive estate plan with a revocable living trust — the probate savings alone deliver a 300-1,000% return. Update your beneficiary designations today (free), review your plan every 3-5 years, and remember: the goal of estate planning is not to create perfect documents. It is to protect the people you love from financial chaos during the worst moment of their lives.

Use it for parsing document images into text and structure, recognizing formulas and tables, answering questions about text-rich images or documents, and extracting structured fields. The exact model is a 0.8B vision-language model based on Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base. Its training recipe uses Q-Mask text anchoring, OCR-centric continued pretraining, and mixed-task reinforcement learning. The source describes an approximately 170M-sample OCR-centric training corpus. Metadata identifies Transformers and Safetensors, and lists the Apache-2.0 license. Reported scores include 97.84 on UniMER-Test for formula recognition, 92.27 on PubTabNet for table recognition, and 73 on Chronicles-OCR Mature Scripts. No hardware, context length, or measured inference performance is supplied for the original checkpoint. The 4B teacher figures in the source describe separate models, not this 0.8B checkpoint.

#9785. Google’s August 2026 Spam Update

Posted on Nov 3 • Originally published at kevinleary.net

The update began August 18, 2026 and completed in roughly 2 days and 16 hours according to Google’s ranking updates dashboard, the second spam update of the year after June’s and the third counting March’s. That rollout speed matters on its own: spam updates used to take a week or more, and a sub-three-day cycle means Google’s spam systems are classifying at a pace where there is no window to notice a drop and react mid-rollout. You find out after it’s done.

Spam updates are improvements to Google’s automated spam detection, the systems behind what Google calls SpamBrain, and they enforce the published spam policies rather than general quality ranking. That distinction matters for diagnosis: a core update rebalances what good content ranks; a spam update removes or demotes content Google has classified as violating policy. There’s no manual action notice in Search Console, no email, and nothing to appeal. Google’s own guidance for affected sites is blunt: review the spam policies, fix what violates them, and expect recovery to take months as the systems revalidate the site, often not fully until a following update.

The spam policies most relevant to legitimate businesses in 2026 are three:

Who feels it most: sites that scaled page count as a strategy. Local service businesses with 200 thin city pages, SaaS companies with auto-generated comparison and glossary fleets, publishers running AI content pipelines with light editing, and affiliates stacking templated reviews. Who generally doesn’t: sites with fewer pages that each carry real expertise, evidence, and a reason to exist.

For years my core recommendation for both SEO and AI answer engines has been consolidation: fewer, denser, more authoritative pages instead of a thin page per keyword variant. Merge the overlapping posts, 301 the losers into the winner, kill the pages that exist only to exist, and make every surviving URL the best available answer to the question it targets. It’s how I’ve approached AEO work long before this update, and the August rollout is Google formally agreeing.

The logic was never mysterious. Authority signals concentrated on one strong page outrank the same signals split across five weak ones, AI assistants citing sources pick the page that answers completely rather than the fragment farm, and every thin page on a domain drags down the classifier’s read of everything else. Scaled content dilutes; consolidation compounds. What changed in August is the penalty side of the ledger: the thin half of your site is no longer just dead weight, it’s a policy liability attached to your domain.

I practice this on my own site, not just client work: overlapping articles get merged and redirected into one canonical piece, templated landing pages get individually written titles, descriptions, and genuinely distinct content or they get removed, and pages with no search or citation value get pruned. The result is a site where every URL can survive a spam classifier looking for scaled patterns, because none of it is scaled.

Recovery from a spam classification does not come from retouching titles on 400 thin pages. The playbook that works:

The uncomfortable summary for businesses: Google spent two and a half days in August enforcing what quality-focused practitioners have said for years, that page count is not a strategy. If your site got hit, the path back is making it smaller and better. If it didn’t, the update is your argument for never letting anyone scale it thin in the first place. Either way, consolidation stopped being a philosophy in August; it’s now the compliance posture.

#9784. Ahrefs vs SEMrush: Which SEO Tool Should You Use?


SEMrush and Ahrefs are among the most popular tools in the SEO industry. Both companies have been in business for years and have thousands of customers per month.

If you're a professional SEO or trying to do digital marketing on your own, at some point you'll likely consider using a tool to help with your efforts. Ahrefs and SEMrush are two names that will likely appear on your shortlist.

In this guide, I'm going to help you learn more about these SEO tools and how to choose the one that's best for your purposes.

What is SEMrush?


SEMrush is a popular SEO tool with a wide range of features—it's the leading competitor research service for online marketers. SEMrush's SEO Keyword Magic tool offers over 20 billion Google-approved keywords, which are constantly updated and it's the largest keyword database.

The program was developed in 2007 as SeoQuake is a small Firefox extension

Features

  • Most accurate keyword data: Accurate keyword search volume data is crucial for SEO and PPC campaigns by allowing you to identify what keywords are most likely to bring in big sales from ad clicks. SEMrush constantly updates its databases and provides the most accurate data.
  • Largest Keyword database: SEMrush's Keyword Magic Tool now features 20-billion keywords, providing marketers and SEO professionals the largest database of keywords.

  • All SEMrush users receive daily ranking data, mobile volume information, and the option to buy additional keywords by default with no additional payment or add-ons needed
  • Most accurate position tracking tool: This tool provides all subscribers with basic tracking capabilities, making it suitable for SEO professionals. Plus, the Position Tracking tool provides local-level data to everyone who uses the tool.
  • SEO Data Management: SEMrush makes managing your online data easy by allowing you to create visually appealing custom PDF reports, including Branded and White Label reports, report scheduling, and integration with GA, GMB, and GSC.
  • Toxic link monitoring and penalty recovery: With SEMrush, you can make a detailed analysis of toxic backlinks, toxic scores, toxic markers, and outreach to those sites.
  • Content Optimization and Creation Tools: SEMrush offers content optimization and creation tools that let you create SEO-friendly content. Some features include the SEO Writing Assistant, On-Page SEO Check, er/SEO Content Template, Content Audit, Post Tracking, Brand Monitoring.

Ahrefs



Ahrefs is a leading SEO platform that offers a set of tools to grow your search traffic, research your competitors, and monitor your niche. The company was founded in 2010, and it has become a popular choice among SEO tools. Ahrefs has a keyword index of over 10.3 billion keywords and offers accurate and extensive backlink data updated every 15-30 minutes and it is the world's most extensive backlink index database.

Features

  • Backlink alerts data and new keywords: Get an alert when your site is linked to or discussed in blogs, forums, comments, or when new keywords are added to a blog posting about you.
  • Intuitive interface: The intuitive design of the widget helps you see the overall health of your website and search engine ranking at a glance.
  • Site Explorer: The Site Explorer will give you an in-depth look at your site's search traffic.
  • Domain Comparison
  • Reports with charts and graphs
  • JavaScript rendering and a site audit can identify SEO issues.
  • A question explorer that provides well-crafted topic suggestions

Direct Comparisons: Ahrefs vs SEMrush

Now that you know a little more about each tool, let's take a look at how they compare. I'll analyze each tool to see how they differ in interfaces, keyword research resources, rank tracking, and competitor analysis.

User Interface

Ahrefs and SEMrush both offer comprehensive information and quick metrics regarding your website's SEO performance. However, Ahrefs takes a bit more of a hands-on approach to getting your account fully set up, whereas SEMrush's simpler dashboard can give you access to the data you need quickly.

In this section, we provide a brief overview of the elements found on each dashboard and highlight the ease with which you can complete tasks.

AHREFS



The Ahrefs dashboard is less cluttered than that of SEMrush, and its primary menu is at the very top of the page, with a search bar designed only for entering URLs.

Additional features of the Ahrefs platform include:

  • You can see analytics from the dashboard, including search engine rankings to domain ratings, referring domains, and backlink
  • Jumping from one tool to another is easy. You can use the Keyword Explorer to find a keyword to target and then directly track your ranking with one click.
  • The website offers a tooltip helper tool that allows you to hover your mouse over something that isn't clear and get an in-depth explanation.

SEMRUSH



When you log into the SEMrush Tool, you will find four main modules. These include information about your domains, organic keyword analysis, ad keyword, and site traffic.

You'll also find some other options like

  • A search bar allows you to enter a domain, keyword, or anything else you wish to explore.
  • A menu on the left side of the page provides quick links to relevant information, including marketing insights, projects, keyword analytics, and more.
  • The customer support resources located directly within the dashboard can be used to communicate with the support team or to learn about other resources such as webinars and blogs.
  • Detailed descriptions of every resource offered. This detail is beneficial for new marketers, who are just starting.

WHO WINS?

Both Ahrefs and SEMrush have user-friendly dashboards, but Ahrefs is less cluttered and easier to navigate. On the other hand, SEMrush offers dozens of extra tools, including access to customer support resources.

When deciding on which dashboard to use, consider what you value in the user interface, and test out both.

Rank Tracking

If you're looking to track your website's search engine ranking, rank tracking features can help. You can also use them to monitor your competitors.

Let's take a look at Ahrefs vs. SEMrush to see which tool does a better job.

Ahrefs



The Ahrefs Rank Tracker is simpler to use. Just type in the domain name and keywords you want to analyze, and it spits out a report showing you the search engine results page (SERP) ranking for each keyword you enter.

Rank Tracker looks at the ranking performance of keywords and compares them with the top rankings for those keywords. Ahrefs also offers:

You'll see metrics that help you understand your visibility, traffic, average position, and keyword difficulty.

It gives you an idea of whether a keyword would be profitable to target or not.

SEMRUSH



SEMRush offers a tool called Position Tracking. This tool is a project tool—you must set it up as a new project. Below are a few of the most popular features of the SEMrush Position Tracking tool:

All subscribers are given regular data updates and mobile search rankings upon subscribing

The platform provides opportunities to track several SERP features, including Local tracking.

Intuitive reports allow you to track statistics for the pages on your website, as well as the keywords used in those pages.

Identify pages that may be competing with each other using the Cannibalization report.

WHO WINS?

Ahrefs is a more user-friendly option. It takes seconds to enter a domain name and keywords. From there, you can quickly decide whether to proceed with that keyword or figure out how to rank better for other keywords.

SEMrush allows you to check your mobile rankings and ranking updates daily, which is something Ahrefs does not offer. SEMrush also offers social media rankings, a tool you won't find within the Ahrefs platform. Both are good which one do you like let me know in the comment.

Keyword Research

Keyword research is closely related to rank tracking, but it's used for deciding which keywords you plan on using for future content rather than those you use now.

When it comes to SEO, keyword research is the most important thing to consider when comparing the two platforms.

AHREFS



The Ahrefs Keyword Explorer provides you with thousands of keyword ideas and filters search results based on the chosen search engine.

Ahrefs supports several features, including:

  • It can search multiple keywords in a single search and analyze them together. At SEMrush, you also have this feature in Keyword Overview.
  • Ahrefs has a variety of keywords for different search engines, including Google, YouTube, Amazon, Bing, Yahoo, Yandex, and other search engines.
  • When you click on a keyword, you can see its search volume and keyword difficulty, but also other keywords related to it, which you didn't use.

SEMRUSH



SEMrush's Keyword Magic Tool has over 20 billion keywords for Google. You can type in any keyword you want, and a list of suggested keywords will appear.

The Keyword Magic Tool also lets you to:

  • Show performance metrics by keyword
  • Search results are based on both broad and exact keyword matches.
  • Show data like search volume, trends, keyword difficulty, and CPC.
  • Show the first 100 Google search results for any keyword.
  • Identify SERP Features and Questions related to each keyword
  • SEMrush has released a new Keyword Gap Tool that uncovers potentially useful keyword opportunities for you, including both paid and organic keywords.

WHO WINS?

Both of these tools offer keyword research features and allow users to break down complicated tasks into something that can be understood by beginners and advanced users alike.

If you're interested in keyword suggestions, SEMrush appears to have more keyword suggestions than Ahrefs does. It also continues to add new features, like the Keyword Gap tool and SERP Questions recommendations.

Competitor Analysis

Both platforms offer competitor analysis tools, eliminating the need to come up with keywords off the top of your head. Each tool is useful for finding keywords that will be useful for your competition so you know they will be valuable to you.

AHREFS



Ahrefs' domain comparison tool lets you compare up to five websites (your website and four competitors) side-by-side.it also shows you how your site is ranked against others with metrics such as backlinks, domain ratings, and more.

Use the Competing Domains section to see a list of your most direct competitors, and explore how many keywords matches your competitors have.

To find more information about your competitor, you can look at the Site Explorer and Content Explorer tools and type in their URL instead of yours.

SEMRUSH



SEMrush provides a variety of insights into your competitors' marketing tactics. The platform enables you to research your competitors effectively. It also offers several resources for competitor analysis including:

Traffic Analytics helps you identify where your audience comes from, how they engage with your site, what devices visitors use to view your site, and how your audiences overlap with other websites.

SEMrush's Organic Research examines your website's major competitors and shows their organic search rankings, keywords they are ranking for, and even if they are ranking for any (SERP) features and more.

The Market Explorer search field allows you to type in a domain and lists websites or articles similar to what you entered. Market Explorer also allows users to perform in-depth data analytics on These companies and markets.

WHO WINS?

SEMrush wins here because it has more tools dedicated to competitor analysis than Ahrefs. However, Ahrefs offers a lot of functionality in this area, too. It takes a combination of both tools to gain an advantage over your competition.

Pricing

Ahrefs

  • Lite Monthly: $99/month
  • Standard Monthly: $179/month
  • Annually Lite: $990/year
  • Annually Standard: $1790/year

SEMRUSH

  • Pro Plan: $119.95/month
  • Guru Plan:$229.95/month
  • Business Plan: $449.95/month

Which SEO tool should you choose for digital marketing?

When it comes to keyword data research, you will become confused about which one to choose.

Consider choosing Ahrefs if you

  • Like friendly and clean interface
  • Searching for simple keyword suggestions

  • Want to get more keywords for different search engines like Amazon, Bing, Yahoo, Yandex, Baidu, and more

 

Consider SEMrush if you:

  • Want more marketing and SEO features
  • Need competitor analysis tool
  • Need to keep your backlinks profile clean
  • Looking for more keyword suggestions for Google

Both tools are great. Choose the one which meets your requirements and if you have any experience using either Ahrefs or SEMrush let me know in the comment section which works well for you.

#9783. Fledge Brings Its Compatibility-Based Matching Model to New York City

TechnologyWire (Technology Wire) is a tech newswire and press release distribution platform operated by MediaFuse LTD.

TechnologyWire (Technology Wire) is a tech newswire and press release distribution platform operated by MediaFuse LTD.

TechnologyWire (Technology Wire) is a tech newswire and press release distribution platform operated by MediaFuse LTD.

New York, United States, November 2nd, 2026/TechnologyWire/--Fledge, a compatibility-based dating platform, is launching in New York City on November 2. It is the founders' second dating product: their previous platform, operating across Europe and the CIS since 2021, has registered more than 20 million users.

According to a Forbes Health survey conducted by OnePoll, 79% of Gen Z and 80% of millennial dating app users report feeling burned out by the swipe-match-ghost cycle. Yet while dating platforms have grown increasingly sophisticated at optimizing engagement, discovery, and time spent in-app, the fundamental mechanism for finding a partner has barely changed: show users more people and let them choose.

Fledge takes the opposite approach. The team has spent years developing technology that identifies compatibility between users based on personality traits and relationship preferences, rather than relying primarily on photos and swiping behavior.

That approach has produced measurable relationship outcomes. A July 2026 survey of users who deleted their profile on the team's previous platform reported that 27% of respondents who went on a date through it said they went on to enter a serious relationship, and thousands of couples reported in 2026 that their relationship led to marriage.

Fledge is built on the premise that successful matching requires understanding compatibility beyond physical attraction and shared interests.

During onboarding, users complete a personality questionnaire drawing on widely used personality frameworks including the Big Five personality traits, along with preferences relevant to relationship compatibility. Fledge then uses these inputs to assess compatibility between users and generate a short list of recommended profiles. Rather than presenting an endless feed, the platform delivers fewer, more relevant recommendations tailored to each person's personality profile.

The algorithm is continuously refined using data and feedback from user interactions, and the company intends to pursue independent research partnerships to further develop its approach to compatibility.

As part of this release, Fledge is introducing an in-app compatibility test tied to its World Connection Day offline events. The test assigns each user a communication-style ribbon color shown during onboarding, which makes it easier to identify and connect with compatible people at in-person Fledge events. It's a first step toward a broader shift for the platform and becoming the first dating app built to power real-world, offline meetups, not just in-app matching.

New York marks Fledge's first U.S. market. The company plans to expand next into Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Miami, followed by other major U.S. cities nationwide. The app itself, however, is already live worldwide — users ready to widen their search beyond their home market can immediately tap into a global base of over 1 million registered members.

Fledge is a dating app designed to help people understand compatibility before they start dating. Going beyond attraction, Fledge uses a research-based approach that considers personality, values, and relationship preferences to identify who may genuinely be a good fit before the first message. The result is fewer, more meaningful matches and a calmer way to date at your own pace, with less pressure, less performance, and more space to be yourself.

Fledge is built by serial entrepreneurs with experience creating dating products used by more than 20 million people, including one of Europe's top 10 dating platforms. Its compatibility model draws on established behavioral science, and the company intends to pursue independent research partnerships. Founded in 2026, Fledge is operated by Fleamily, Inc., a Delaware corporation based in New York. For more information, visit fledge.love

#9782. The Case for Ungating Your Most Useful B2B Content

Founder and CEO of INSIDEA. Writing about HubSpot, RevOps, CRM architecture, AI, and the systems behind reliable growth.

Founder and CEO of INSIDEA. Writing about HubSpot, RevOps, CRM architecture, AI, and the systems behind reliable growth.

Founder and CEO of INSIDEA. Writing about HubSpot, RevOps, CRM architecture, AI, and the systems behind reliable growth.

Hero image: Original AI-assisted illustration created for this article.

A buyer clicks a guide promising to explain a difficult implementation decision. The page asks for a work email before revealing whether the guide contains anything useful. The form may create a contact, but it also interrupts the very evaluation the content was supposed to support.

That tradeoff deserves testing, not a universal rule. Some resources justify registration. Others earn more value by being accessible enough to discover, reference, share, and use before a commercial conversation begins.

Disclosure: I am the founder and CEO of INSIDEA, an Elite HubSpot Partner. This article reflects practical experience and independent research. It is not sponsored by HubSpot or any other company mentioned.

I would evaluate content gates by the job of the resource and the relationship requested in return. The proposal below is an experiment design for B2B teams, not a prediction that removing every form will improve revenue or guarantee inclusion in AI answers.

A form can perform several jobs: deliver an asset, create an account, register someone for an event, request a consultation, or ask permission for continuing communication. Those purposes should not be silently bundled into a single download action.

State what the person receives and what relationship they are initiating. A buyer seeking a reference diagram may not be requesting a sales call. A person booking a tailored workshop is making a different choice and may reasonably need to provide more context.

Design the exchange around that distinction. Public educational material can help someone understand an issue, while an optional next step offers a deeper interaction. The useful question is not whether a form exists. It is whether the value and the requested commitment are proportionate and clearly explained.

Start with the resource's primary job. A definition, implementation checklist, or reference model often needs to be encountered before a buyer knows whom to trust. A personalized assessment or live event may require information to deliver the promised experience.

Do not assume that a long PDF is valuable simply because it took effort to produce. Evaluate whether the asset provides original evidence, a usable method, or a decision aid. Length is not a substitute for utility, and registration is not evidence of commercial intent.

Google's people-first content guidance provides a usefulness-oriented reference point. Apply that review to both the landing page and the resource. A polished promise followed by a generic document creates friction without delivering a meaningful exchange.

Public access, crawlability, indexing eligibility, and actual appearance in search are separate states. Removing a form does not guarantee that a page is technically accessible or selected for a search feature. Keeping a gate does not make every implementation invisible by definition.

Google documents markup for paywalled and registration content. Supported implementation details matter; a blanket claim that all gated material cannot be indexed would be inaccurate.

Work with the website owner to inspect the actual delivery path. Is useful text available on the page? What does an unauthenticated reader receive? Are important resources blocked unintentionally? Does the visible description accurately represent what follows? Do not solve an editorial access problem with speculative technical claims about every crawler or answer engine.

Original AI-assisted illustration created for this article.

One option is to make the method public while offering additional value through a deliberate relationship. Publish the explanation and a usable example. Offer a customized review, a live discussion, or an optional subscription separately.

For a hypothetical CRM migration guide, the public resource could explain acceptance tests and provide a blank checklist. A scoped consultation could evaluate the buyer's actual environment. Those are different services; the consultation does not need to be disguised as delivery of a file.

Avoid fragmenting the public resource so aggressively that it cannot answer the reader's question. A teaser that withholds every practical detail is still a gate in effect. The core should be useful without the optional step, while the next interaction offers something meaningfully different.

A form count is an observable operational metric. It does not establish that the contacts are suitable buyers or that the resource contributed to a purchase. Removing the gate may reduce form submissions while improving access; neither direction alone settles the business case.

Define a measurement ladder: resource access, meaningful use where measurable, voluntary next steps, qualified conversations, and opportunity outcomes. Explain what each event represents and what remains unobserved. A copied worksheet may be valuable without creating a measurable session every time it is used.

Google's AI search guidance keeps established SEO practices relevant. Access decisions should support useful discoverable content, but they should not be sold internally as a guaranteed shortcut to AI citations. Treat discovery effects as outcomes to observe, not benefits already proven by the change.

Choose a narrow asset type and define the decision before starting. Compare alternatives that differ in a way the team can interpret. For example, one experience might provide the full guide publicly with an optional worksheet request, while another uses the existing registration process.

Decide how traffic will be allocated, how long observation will continue, what qualifies as a meaningful next step, and which outcomes are too sparse for a reliable conclusion. Keep other changes limited where practical. If the company launches a major campaign halfway through the test, record it rather than attributing all movement to the gate.

The experiment should protect the reader experience. Do not use deceptive promises, hide obligations, or change communication preferences merely to increase measured conversions. The test is intended to compare value delivery and relationship formation, not to find a more effective way to surprise visitors.

A student, a competitor, a consultant, and a potential customer may all want the same guide. That is not necessarily a failure of the content. Educational resources can serve audiences beyond immediate buyers while building a useful public body of knowledge.

Separate content interest from fit and readiness. A contact who asks for a reference document should not automatically be described as a qualified lead. Define qualification through the organization's actual process, and preserve the distinction in CRM reporting.

Where follow-up is appropriate, use the permissions and preferences attached to that relationship. The existence of contact information is not by itself an instruction to start an automated outreach sequence. Explain the intended next step clearly and use the organization's approved communication rules.

B2B evaluation often involves more than one person. A public reference can be shared with a technical reviewer, finance colleague, or project owner without asking each recipient to repeat a form. That is a plausible benefit worth investigating, not a measured effect assumed in advance.

Design the resource so it remains understandable when shared out of context. Use a clear title, visible date, definitions, limitations, and a stable location. Keep the contact path available without allowing it to dominate the educational material.

HubSpot's AI visibility guidance discusses content discovery and brand presence. The public resource should still earn its place through usefulness. A page made accessible solely to repeat promotional claims is not a substitute for evidence a buying committee can inspect.

Ungating is not cost-free. Public templates need maintenance, support boundaries, and clear limitations. If the resource is technical, explain what a reader must verify before applying it. Avoid implying that a generic checklist replaces account-specific implementation work.

Likewise, gating creates operational work: form reliability, delivery, duplicate records, consent handling, follow-up, and support when the asset does not arrive. Include those costs when comparing approaches. The cost of the original document is only one part of the system.

Assign an owner for the resource after release. When the method changes, update the public version and affected derivatives. A broken download or obsolete checklist undermines both models. Access strategy cannot compensate for a resource that stops being accurate after its launch campaign ends.

Use, voluntary next steps and support load

Attendance and explicitly chosen follow-up

The table is a planning aid, not a rule that all assets in a row should receive the same treatment. Consider the audience, confidentiality, commercial model, and delivery requirements. Document the reason for the choice so future reviewers can tell whether the conditions have changed.

A public worksheet can travel farther than its original landing page. Include enough context within the file or page for a new reader to understand its intended use, assumptions, review date, and limitations. The fact that a resource is free does not reduce the need to maintain it.

For a hypothetical migration checklist, distinguish a planning aid from an executable migration procedure. Explain that account-specific mappings, access, backups, and acceptance tests need separate verification. A reader should not infer that completing a generic worksheet proves production readiness.

Likewise, make the optional commercial step specific. Explain whether the request is for a discussion, an assessment, or a delivered service. Do not use an apparently educational invitation to obscure an automatic outreach sequence or a commitment the person did not understand.

The experiment should examine these experiences as well as conversion counts. Review whether readers receive what was promised, whether internal teams can respond appropriately, and whether the resource helps clarify the decision. A larger contact database is not a sufficient outcome if the resulting relationships begin with confusion. A smaller set of deliberate requests can be valuable, but that possibility must be measured rather than asserted as a guaranteed benefit of ungating.

Begin with one resource whose gate seems difficult to justify. Establish a baseline, improve the public experience, and observe the results with qualification and measurement limits intact. Do not remove every form or declare victory because page visits rise.

The business objective is not maximum anonymity or maximum contact capture. It is a useful exchange that helps appropriate buyers make progress and choose a relationship when they are ready. Public access and intentional conversion can support each other when their jobs are clearly separated.

The future of B2B content may involve more discovery through intermediaries. That makes the access decision worth revisiting. It does not remove the need to deliver something worth finding in the first place.

For a related evidence boundary, see Your HubSpot Attribution Report Is Not a Revenue Ledger. The framework above addresses a distinct marketing decision rather than repeating that model.

Sources checked October 21, 2026. Proposed experiments are illustrative and do not establish expected conversion, ranking, or revenue effects.

#9781. Autonomous DNS for Autonomous Code: Inside LovieMe v0.6.0

Posted on Nov 3 • Originally published at sagarithm.in

Over the last 18 months, software development workflows underwent a historic transformation. With tools like Cursor, Claude Code, and Antigravity, scaffolding a complete production web application takes minutes.

Yet, despite this quantum leap, the deployment edge remained trapped in the early 2000s.

Once an agent finishes drafting an application, the developer is still forced to:

Software engineering cannot reach true end-to-end autonomy as long as domain registration and DNS routing require manual browser clicks.

Today, we are launching LovieMe v0.6.0—a complete AI-native subdomain and Anycast DNS platform engineered from the ground up for both human engineers and autonomous AI agents.

The cornerstone of the v0.6.0 release is our native Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, packaged as lovieme-mcp.

Add it to your Cursor or Claude Code configuration:

The MCP server exposes 5 deterministic tools:

When an AI assistant builds a micro-SaaS demo, it can now claim agent-tracker.lovie.me, wire up Cloudflare or Vercel routing, and provide the user with a verified live edge URL directly in chat.

For terminal-first engineers, npx lovie eliminates GUI friction entirely:

The CLI features interactive browser OAuth for local terminal sessions and headless token support (LOVIE_API_KEY) for Docker containers and continuous integration pipelines.

Granting autonomous agents infrastructure access poses security hazards. If an untrusted agent or compromised script gains full administrative access, your entire zone is at risk.

LovieMe solves this with One-Way Cryptographic Tokens & Subdomain Sandboxing:

Manual DNS configuration is notoriously error-prone. LovieMe provides 1-Click Verified Cloud Presets:

Instead of waiting blindly, LovieMe queries global DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) backbones in parallel:

The diagnostic engine confirms sub-2-second global propagation across North America, Europe, and Asia empirically.

Teams waste hours cleaning up stale test domains. The official GitHub Action (lovieme/action@v1) automates the full lifecycle:

When a PR is opened, a dedicated subdomain is created. When the PR is merged or closed, the subdomain is automatically deleted.

Under DNS standards (RFC 1034 section 3.6.2 and RFC 2181), if a CNAME record exists at a node, no other data records may exist at that node. Setting an A record alongside a CNAME causes silent resolution failure (SERVFAIL) across major resolvers.

LovieMe's Conflict Engine inspects RRsets prior to persistence, blocks illegal collisions at the API perimeter, and surfaces one-click automated repair workflows to keep your edge records healthy.

Modern infrastructure should match the speed of the models generating our software.

Built by Sagar Kewat. What edge DNS challenges are you facing with your AI agents? Let me know in the comments!

#9779. Corporate PowerPoint decks with AI, for free: slides as code, QA as the gate

Ask an AI chat to "make me a board deck" and you usually get one of three things:

I wanted a fourth option: the AI writes the deck, a machine proves it is correct, and a second AI with fresh eyes judges it. That project is PowerPoint Factory. It is MIT-licensed and you can clone it today.

The sample: a 20-slide Q4 board review for Halden Logistics, a fictional company. Every shape, chart and table is native and editable in PowerPoint.

Every slide is a small typed recipe, one file per slide. You pick a layout by the message you want to land, not by where boxes go:

That becomes this. Real shapes, not an image:

This is why AI is good at it. An LLM is bad at pixel geometry and good at structured data. Layouts handle the geometry, so the model only has to get the content and the story right.

There are 23 built-in layouts: cover, agenda, summary, stats, chart, waterfall, table (with RAG status and Harvey balls), 2×2 matrix, process, timeline, roadmap, next steps, references and more. Charts (column, bar, stacked, line, area, pie, doughnut) are native PowerPoint charts, so finance can still click in and fix a number.

Generating a .pptx is easy. Generating one you would send to a board is not. So every build runs about 40 checks, and each one comes with a → fix hint the agent can act on:

The output folder gives you, and the agent, everything needed to look at the result: a contact sheet, one PNG per slide, a QA report, and an outline containing only the titles. If the titles alone don't tell the story, the deck isn't done.

The /deck command follows the same workflow a consultant would:

The agent is also told never to invent facts. A missing number becomes a TBD in the speaker notes and is listed back to you. It never ends up on a slide, and QA fails if one does.

Stock photos are where a lot of corporate decks die: the same handshake, the same glass tower, and a license nobody checked. The factory gets its imagery from Kubeez instead, and it's what makes the sample deck look like an agency made it:

Every photo in the Halden deck is a Kubeez generation, including the cover and the warehouse shots.

Why it fits a slides-as-code workflow so well:

In a recipe, an image is just a prop. The factory generates it on the first build and reads it from the cache after that. Add KUBEEZ_API_KEY to .env and you're set.

Each company gets a "brand brain": BRAND.md for voice, logo rules, colors and approved facts, brand.ts for theme tokens, plus logos and reusable photos. Four built-in themes (cobalt, ledger, graphite, terracotta) all pass a WCAG AA test, and extendTheme puts your colors on top. A brand-reviewer agent checks claims and logo use against BRAND.md before anything ships.

Pick one motion profile per deck: none (for read-ahead decks), subtle (the default, a fade transition), build (click reveals) or keynote (Morph). Per-slide effect soup isn't an option.

If you build a deck with it, I'd like to see the contact sheet. Drop it in the comments.
